Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleMedia Corp Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your telephone keypad if you would like to join the queue. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleMedia Corp's Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Network Officer; David Kim, Chief Commercial Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3, demonstrating our continued commitment to growth and innovation. Our success is driven by our dedicated team and strategic investments.

Our key achievements include significant network investments in 5G deployment and capital expenditures, robust EBITDA margin expansion through key drivers and trends, effective operating expense management initiatives boosting profitability, sustainable dividends and strong shareholder returns, favorable cost of revenue trends and drivers, impactful new product and service launches driving revenue and subscriber growth, prudent debt levels and leverage ratios, and impressive free cash flow generation and utilization. The launch of NovaStream Ultra is exceeding expectations, resulting in substantial subscriber adds and ARPU uplift. Further milestones include nationwide 5G coverage gains and media synergies. We are also focusing on AI-driven efficiencies and partnerships. Our dedication to customer experience and sustainability is bearing fruit. Our strategy is to enhance converged telecom-media offerings. We are actively investing in edge computing and Open RAN. We are also exploring 5G-Advanced trials and finally, analyzing balance sheet strength for long-term value.

With that, I'll turn it over to Jordan for a deeper dive into our financial results.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. Now, let's review our financial performance. Revenue for the quarter reached $28.7 billion, reflecting a 4% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.2 billion, resulting in a margin of 39.2%. We maintain a disciplined approach to cost management and capital allocation. Capital expenditures totaled $2.1 billion, primarily allocated to expanding our 5G network, fiber infrastructure, and content investments.

Let me dive deeper into some of these areas starting with our EBITDA margin performance, which came in at 38.2% for the quarter—up 320 basis points year-over-year from 35.0% in Q3 2022, and 110 basis points sequentially from Q2 2023's 37.1%. This marks our strongest quarterly margin in three years and puts us ahead of the industry composite of 36.5% as reported by Dell'Oro Group for North American telcos. On a trailing 12-month basis, our margin now stands at 37.8%, reflecting consistent operational leverage from our wireless ARPU growth, media subscriber ramps, and cost efficiencies across the board.

Turning to operating expense management initiatives and their impact on profitability, these have been a cornerstone of our profitability enhancement strategy. In an industry facing persistent inflationary pressures on labor, energy, and content acquisition—exacerbated by ongoing 5G spectrum auctions and intensifying streaming wars—we've delivered $450 million in year-to-date OpEx savings, directly contributing to that 320 basis point expansion in our Adjusted EBITDA margin to 38.2%, up from 35% last year. This not only offset a 7% rise in network energy costs due to our aggressive 5G Standalone rollout but also positions us to return over $1.2 billion to shareholders via buybacks and dividends in the second half.

Breaking it down, our largest bucket of savings came from network operations and infrastructure optimization, totaling $220 million year-to-date, or 49% of total OpEx reductions. We've accelerated our shift to virtualized and cloud-native architectures, leveraging Ericsson's Cloud RAN and Nokia's AirScale portfolio to reduce physical hardware costs. Predictive maintenance via AI and machine learning models across our 5G core predicted 85% of fiber optic faults before outages, cutting unplanned maintenance costs by 28%, or $85 million. Energy optimization involved retrofitting 40% of macro sites with solar-hybrid backups and dynamic spectrum sharing, slashing energy OpEx by $65 million—22% per site in North America and 31% in Europe thanks to EU Green Deal tailwinds. Vendor consolidation with Huawei and Samsung achieved 12-15% volume discounts on backhaul equipment, saving $70 million. These efforts lowered our Cost of Services excluding depreciation to 42% of revenue, down from 45% year-over-year.

In our Media segment, generating $2.8 billion in quarterly revenue from streaming and linear assets, we clawed back $120 million through smarter rights management. Tiered content bundling shifted 25% of premium sports rights to ad-supported tiers, reducing amortization by 18% or $50 million, boosting direct-to-consumer ARPU by 8% to $14.50. In-house production scaling with AI tools like Adobe Sensei cut outsourced editing by $40 million, especially in APAC with localized content. Affiliate fee resets with MVPDs like Charter yielded $30 million.

SG&A came in at $1.1 billion, down 11% year-over-year, via zero-based budgeting, RPA automating 60% of back-office tasks saving $45 million, workforce optimization with AI chatbots handling 70% of Tier 1 queries for $35 million, and real estate consolidation saving $30 million. Emerging markets delivered outsized leverage. These are part of our Efficiency Engine 2.0 framework, targeting $600 million more in 2025 savings, with Adjusted EBITDA up 14% to $3.2 billion and free cash flow conversion at 48%.

On cost of revenue, which was $6.8 billion for the quarter or 52% of total revenue—a 120 basis point improvement year-over-year from 53.2% and flat sequentially—this marks our 11th straight quarter of discipline amid 12% top-line growth from 5G and streaming. Cost of revenue grew 8% to $6.8 billion. Network operations at $3.25 billion, up 7%, with unit costs per GB down 15%. Content at $2.1 billion, up 12%, offset by ad tiers. CPE and installation at $850 million, up 3%, and spectrum at $600 million, up 5%.

Drivers include 28% YoY mobile data surge to 4.2 EB from 5G Ultra Wideband covering 85% of top 100 markets, adding $450 million in bandwidth; media consumption pushing CDN up 14%; energy up 9% or $120 million; depreciation up $200 million to $1.1 billion from $4.2 billion capex. Offsets from 10% CPE drop to $45 per sub. North America grew 6%, Europe 15% due to regs, APAC flat. AI optimization saved $150 million, vRAN targeting 50% footprint by 2025. Q3 guide $6.9-7.0 billion or 51-52%.

Regarding dividend sustainability and shareholder returns, we declared a quarterly dividend of $0.50 per share, or $2.00 annualized, our 18th consecutive year of increases, yielding 4.5% at $44.25 share price—above S&P average and in line with peers. Payout ratio 58% of $3.45 adjusted EPS, FCF coverage 1.65x on $8.4 billion generated versus $5.1 billion dividends. Telecom optimizations like C-band nearing 95% coverage unlocked $1.2 billion FCF; media with 85 million GCOM+ subs added $2.8 billion FCF. Leverage 2.1x gives firepower. Committing $10 billion returns: $5.1 billion dividends, $4.9 billion buybacks, repurchasing 45 million shares YTD. FCF growth 7-9% to $9.0-9.3 billion supports 5% dividend growth.

On debt levels and leverage, total gross debt $118.4 billion, net $106.1 billion against $44.7 billion TTM EBITDA for 2.37x ratio, down 85 bps year-over-year. YTD $18.9 billion FCF deployed $12.4 billion to paydowns. North America 2.1x, Europe 2.6x post tower sale, emerging 3.4x. Refinanced $7 billion green bonds at 4.25%, capex flat at $14.2 billion YTD, media ARPU up 9%. Guide 2.3-2.4x year-end, 2025 FCF $22-24 billion for deleveraging.

Finally, free cash flow for 2023 on track at $4.8 billion, up 18% from $4.1 billion, from $12.6 billion operating cash flow. Wireless $8.2 billion on 4.2% ARPU to $58.70; media $4.4 billion on 15% subs to 28 million. Capex $7.8 billion at 14.5% intensity. North America $3.75 billion, Europe $720 million, APAC $385 million. Conversion 38%. Utilization: 42% or $2.0 billion debt reduction to $48 billion; 35% or $1.7 billion returns ($900 million dividends, $800 million buybacks); 23% or $1.1 billion reinvested in spectrum, media M&A, Open RAN. Guide $5.2-5.6 billion for 2024.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Jordan. I'm pleased to provide an update on our network advancements. We've significantly expanded our 5G coverage, delivering faster speeds and lower latency. Our network reliability remains high, and we are continuously optimizing our infrastructure to meet growing demand. We are also focusing on enhancing our cybersecurity posture. We are committed to architecting an intelligent edge network that powers immersive media experiences from ultra-HD streaming to AR/VR and cloud gaming.

Total capex was $2.1 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with $1.4 billion or 67% to NextGen Network, primarily 5G, spectrum, small cells. Full year $8.2-8.5 billion, 65-70% 5G; 2024 $7.5-8.0 billion down 7-10% via virtualization and Open RAN. We've hit 92% population coverage for 250 million, up from 78%, with 18,000 new sites YTD, 4,200 in Q3, total 85,000 sites. 5G 45% traffic, up 150% YoY; 28 million 5G subs, 62% postpaid, $4.50 ARPU uplift.

NSA 5G with DSS in 2.5 GHz refarmed; SA live in 15 MSAs like NYC, LA, Chicago for slicing—pilots with Disney 8K, AWS edge. 65% new RAN 64T64R massive MIMO from Ericsson, Nokia core; 15% ORAN saving 20-25% OpEx by 2025. U.S. 98% coverage Northeast/California, 450 Mbps speeds; Midwest 1,800 sites IoT; rural 1,200 FWA towers, 2 million homes, 450k subs at $65 ARPU, 40% margins. Latin America $315 million capex, 65% coverage Sao Paulo/Mexico City, JV Claro for Globo bundles.

5G traffic 35% QoQ, mobile data revenue +18% to $2.8 billion; NexaStream 22% subs to 15 million, 30% CDN savings. $450 million capex efficiencies YTD, spectral efficiency +25% Release 16 URLLC <10ms. Preparing Release 18 RedCap/XR with Meta; 50,000 small cells; Qualcomm X80, Samsung mmWave. Payback under 24 months, margins to 42% 2024.

David Kim: Thank you, Maria. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We've seen strong subscriber growth across our various service offerings. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority, and we are continuously improving the customer experience. We are also focused on expanding our partnerships to offer bundled services and enhance customer value. We are prioritizing converged offerings like NovaStream Ultra, 5G Flex Home, and AI Edge Media Suite.

These drove 18% YoY revenue growth to $4.7 billion in Consumer Mobility and Media, $1.2 billion direct lift or 25% of segment. Record 2.8 million net adds, total base 145 million up 7%, ARPU +4.2% to $58.30, churn 0.9%.

NovaStream Ultra at $14.99 or $9.99 bundled: $450 million activation + $120 million RMR from 1.2 million subs, 150% QoQ ramp, 65% margins via Warner JV. 1.2 million adds, 40% cord-cutters, 25% 18-34 share US, 250k Europe Vodafone. Zero-rated 5G data cuts churn 15%.

5G Flex Home FWA: $380 million, $250 million from 850k lines at $70 ARPU. 850k adds, 60% rural US, 200k APAC Singtel, total 3.2 million up 200% YoY. O-RAN capex $1,200/home, 45% EBITDA.

AI Edge Media Suite B2B: $370 million, 80% SaaS ARR $1.1 billion up 90% QoQ. 750k endpoints, 15k SMB. North America 85%, Europe 10%, APAC 5% explosive India Airtel.

Bundling 2.5x LTV; Q4 $1.5 billion incremental, 3.5 million adds. Executing in $1.8 trillion industry.

Raj Patel: Thank you, David. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to transform our business. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations, improve customer service, and develop new products and services. We are also investing in research and development to stay ahead of the curve. Our technological direction is centered on 5G-Advanced, vRAN, and AI orchestration for edge media and enterprise slicing.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Raj. Operationally, we are focused on improving efficiency and streamlining our processes. We are leveraging data analytics to optimize our resource allocation and improve decision-making. We are also committed to sustainability and reducing our environmental impact. Our operational focus is embedding Efficiency Engine 2.0 across network, content, and SG&A for ongoing leverage amid inflation and growth.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your content strategy and your plans for investing in original programming, and what is the anticipated impact on subscriber growth and ARPU?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, John. Our content strategy emphasizes tiered bundling and in-house production to combat streaming wars. We've shifted premium sports to ad-supported, saving on amortization while boosting ARPU 8% to $14.50. NovaStream Ultra with originals via AI curation added 1.2 million subs, 40% from cord-cutters. Originals investments like Atlanta studios expansion cut costs  $40 million, targeting 22% media growth. Anticipated impact: 3-4 million adds in 2024, ARPU +5% from bundles, closing gap on leaders.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for addressing the digital divide and ensuring that all communities have access to affordable broadband, and how do you plan to achieve nationwide coverage goals?

David Kim: Great question, Emily. We're tackling the digital divide head-on with 5G Flex Home FWA, deploying 1,200 rural towers under RDOF, passing 2 million homes and adding 450k subs at $65 ARPU. Targeting BEAD grants for 30 million FTTH by 2025 at 20% lower costs. Partnerships like Singtel in APAC and Claro in LatAm extend affordable $70/month broadband at 450 Mbps. Plan achieves 95% coverage by 2025 via C-band/mmWave, O-RAN efficiencies, positioning for $42 billion grants.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson: Can you discuss your capital allocation priorities and your plans for returning capital to shareholders, including buyback authorization expansion?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, Mike. Priorities balance growth and returns: capex discipline to $7.5-8.0 billion in 2024, deleveraging to 2.3x, then shareholder value. $10 billion over next 12 months: $5.1 billion dividends at 1.65x FCF coverage, $4.9 billion buybacks under expanded $15 billion program—45 million shares YTD. FCF $5.2-5.6 billion supports 5% dividend growth, bolt-ons. Fortress balance sheet enables top-quartile 8.2% yield.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong: What are your strategies for navigating the changing regulatory landscape?

Alex Rivera: Lisa, regulatory agility is key. We've navigated FCC auctions securing 160 MHz C-band, EU Gigabit Act via unbundled access, and emerging market hurdles like Brazil spectrum. Strategies: divest non-core like $4.5 billion rural cable, green bonds for ESG, partnerships for RDOF/BEAD. Open RAN reduces vendor risks, AI compliance for GDPR. Positions us for 6G/metaverse amid scrutiny.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our performance this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainability. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
